transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Julia Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Anna Lopez (CISO, Firstline), Mark Reynolds (Head of Cloud, Firstline), Priya Singh (Compliance), Tom Alvarez (Dev Lead)

Summary (auto): quick discovery focused on data residency needs and compliance requirements for PII and financial records. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; primary concerns: GDPR cross-border, HIPAA for their health-related financial products, audit logs retention and redaction, KMS/HSM integration, and network isolation (VPC/on-prem). Next step is security pack + Dedicated pricing and an infra deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Julia: hey everyone thanks for joining uh i'll kick us off i'm julia from Redwood inference, this is samir our solutions engineer, sound good?
[00:06] Anna: yep thanks, anna here, ciso at Firstline. we have a few people on the call, appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:10] Samir: great thanks anna, can you give us a quick picture of the use cases and what's driving the residency conversation?
[00:16] Mark: sure, we're rolling out a document processing feature for mortgage and some health-linked products. some of the records include PHI and obviously payment data. our legal team flagged residency and audit as blockers for hosted service without clear controls.
[00:28] Priya: yes HIPAA is a hard requirement for the health-adjacent flows. for EU customers we need GDPR compliance and data staying in region unless there's explicit consent and DPA clauses.
[00:37] Tom: also we're trying to avoid long-term logging of full request bodies in case we capture SSNs or similar. we want to understand redwood's logging / retention model.
[00:45] Julia: that's perfect, that's exactly what we expect to cover. at a high level we offer three deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in a customer-isolated tenant), and Private (VPC or on-prem installation). each has different controls—Dedicated gives network and tenancy isolation and Private gives full control over where data lives.
[00:59] Anna: can you explain in plain terms: for Hosted what goes to redwood-office storage? is prompt text persisted in any logs?
[01:07] Samir: yeah so for Hosted, by default we persist request/response logs for 30 days for debugging and observability but we have configurable redaction policies and can enable PII scrubbing on ingest. for regulated customers we often move to Dedicated or Private where log retention and encryption keys are controlled by the customer.
[01:26] Mark: when you say customer-controlled keys, do you support external KMS or HSM? we use AWS KMS and have an HSM-backed flow for some services.
[01:33] Samir: yes we integrate with external KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs via KMIP in the Private piece). for Dedicated we can offer BYOK so the encryption at rest uses keys in your KMS.
[01:44] Priya: how about audit logs—are admin actions and access logged and exportable? our auditors want immutable logs and retention for seven years in some cases.
[01:53] Julia: audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has operational logs but we can provide export options, and for enterprise there's an add-on for long-term retention and log streaming to customer S3 or SIEM. note there are limits on what we stream by default to reduce PII exposure; we'll discuss export and redaction rules.
[02:11] Anna: GDPR note—if a request contains EU person data and it's routed to a non-EU region, is that automatically blocked? we need strong controls there.
[02:19] Samir: we have geo-routing policies. you can pin model endpoints to regions and restrict routing by policy. in Hosted you can request region-specific tenancy but for strict guarantees we recommend Dedicated in the target region or Private on-prem/EU cloud.
[02:33] Tom: any chance of mis-classifying tokens? i mean if we use streaming responses do partial transcripts get logged?
[02:39] Samir: streaming is supported and logs can be gated. we can turn off request/response capture for endpoints used for PHI, and enable real-time redaction or prefix caching that avoids persisting sensitive tokens. there's a tradeoff because disabling logging reduces our ability to debug model regressions.
[02:56] Mark: curious about network: for Dedicated do we get VPC peering or private connectivity?
[03:01] Samir: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private connectivity with AWS PrivateLink; Private gives you full VPC deployment or on-prem bundle. connections are TLS and mutual-TLS optional for Private.
[03:12] Anna: one of the tougher asks is tokenization/pseudonymization before data leaves our environment. can your SDK do client-side pseudonymization?
[03:20] Julia: our SDK supports client-side pre-processing hooks and we have a recommended pattern where sensitive fields are replaced with stable tokens and reversed locally. that works well when you want to keep deterministic behavior without sending raw values. we'll share a pattern doc.
[03:31] Priya: how about data subject requests under GDPR—if a user asks to be forgotten, can you purge their records?
[03:36] Samir: yes for Dedicated and Private we can run purges on request; for Hosted we have a data retention/erasure workflow but it needs coordination. we also help with DPA clauses.
[03:45] Anna: auditors will ask for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and penetration test cadence. do you have those reports?
[03:51] Julia: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we also run regular pentests and can share a summary redacted report. i'll attach the security pack after the call. link to docs: https://redwood.ai/security (note: link shared in chat).
[04:04] Mark: one more: logging restrictions—if our legal says no retention of request bodies longer than 24 hours and no full request in logs at all, can you comply?
[04:13] Samir: on Dedicated/Private absolutely. on Hosted we can sometimes accommodate via contract and configuration but Dedicated is the safer bet if legal mandates short retention windows or zero-body logging.
[04:24] Tom: okay from engineering perspective we need latency and throughput numbers. if we move to Dedicated in eu-west-1 what kind of p99 and tokens/sec can we expect?
[04:33] Samir: it'll depend on model and quantization. for a medium LLM in 8-bit quant with our batching we typically see p50 ~70-150ms and p99 in the 300-700ms range for <2k tokens, but we'll need to run a benchmark on your exact prompts. we'll include a sample benchmark and a guidance sheet.
[04:50] Priya: encryption in transit and at rest—does Redwood support customer-controlled certs?
[04:55] Samir: yes for Private you can bring your certs; for Dedicated we support custom certs and mTLS in most topologies.
[05:02] Anna: about SIEM integration—can we stream audit logs to Splunk?
[05:06] Julia: yes we have log streaming to S3, SIEMs like Splunk or Datadog, and webhooks for events. for high-regulated customers we usually provision a dedicated log export pipeline.
[05:16] Mark: is there any chance of model weights or checkpoints being accessed by Redwood engineers? we need role separation.
[05:22] Samir: we have RBAC and separation of duties; only a limited ops team has access to runtime metrics and only under strict change control. for Private deployments that's fully controlled by you. we can outline the access matrix.
[05:34] Anna: liability and breach notification—what's your SLA and notification timelines?
[05:39] Julia: we publish our SLA for Dedicated/private customers and include breach notification timelines in enterprise agreements—typically 72 hours for high-impact incidents, but we can align contractually.
[05:50] Tom: technical nit: you mentioned KV cache earlier—our workload is heavy on real-time session context, how is cache persistence handled in Dedicated?
[05:57] Samir: KV cache is in-memory per-runtime; in Dedicated it's isolated per customer and we can configure hottest-session cache sizing; if you need sticky sessions we support that too.
[06:10] Priya: one of our requirements is seven-year audit retention for certain records. you said that was an add-on; how is cost structured?
[06:17] Julia: long retention is an add-on with S3 export or warehousing. cost depends on retention size and frequency; we'll include a cost example in the pricing doc.
[06:26] Mark: ok i'm going to flag a couple of blockers: 1) EU residency guarantee for EU customer data 2) BYOK w/ AWS KMS and HSM support 3) no full-body logs in Hosted by default. can you satisfy all three in Dedicated or Private?
[06:38] Samir: yes Dedicated in eu-west or Private on your cloud will meet those—BYOK works, and logging can be disabled/filtered. Hosted would need contractual changes and stronger assurances.
[06:48] Anna: how long to set up Dedicated for a pilot? we want a small pilot for 6 weeks.
[06:53] Julia: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for a Dedicated slice depending on capacity and contract. Private on-prem will take longer. for the pilot we can do a Dedicated pilot in eu-west-1 in ~3 weeks if you sign the MSA.
[07:04] Tom: one last thing, can we run an on-prem benchmark with your runtime on our infra?
[07:09] Samir: yes for Private that's supported; for Dedicated we can run a remote benchmark from our cluster and also provide the benchmark harness to run locally. we'll schedule the infra deep dive to scope this.
[07:18] Priya: thanks, this is helpful. auditors will also want the DPA and data processing addendum.
[07:23] Julia: i'll include the DPA template in the security pack.
[07:26] Mark: recap—please send security pack, Dedicated pricing & sizing, and let's lock the infra deep dive for 10/01.
[07:33] Julia: will do. any other Qs?
[07:36] Anna: not from me, thanks.
[07:38] Tom: thanks everyone.
[07:40] Julia: great we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with docs and proposed calendar invites.

End of transcript.
